label: The denoised guess across sampling steps
context: Two panels side by side (stacked on narrow widths). Left 'image model': a small 12×12 pixel picture; across a step counter going from step 1 to step 50 (accelerated), show the predicted clean image x̂ at the current step: early steps a blurry average, gradually sharpening, with content appearing late. Below it a curve of 'change in x̂ per step' that decays slowly. Right 'co-folding model': a 2D protein-like chain of 30 beads; show its predicted x̂ at each step: already at step 1 x̂ is almost the final shape (only tiny jitter afterwards), while the noisy state x itself (faint) contracts from noise. Below it the 'change in x̂ per step' curve drops to near zero after the first step. Caption: 'in co-folding models x̂ is nearly final at the first step: the open question my thesis studies'. Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 400 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas, and on narrow widths stack or shrink rather than overlap. Loop forever on a cycle of 10 to 16 s with smooth easing between phases. White background. Put a one-line phase caption at the top centre that changes with the phase. No title inside the canvas (the card has one). Use plain sans-serif labels.

spec.title: The denoised guess x̂ across sampling steps
spec.caption: Schematic, not measured data. An image model's denoised prediction starts as a blurred average and changes over many steps. In co-folding models it is close to the final structure from the first step on (Quast et al., 2026). This is the observation my thesis starts from.
